`qm::ThreadPool` is implemented, but one ThreadSanitizer (TSan) report remains that I couldn't remove without a suppression. It's a libstdc++ false positive, explained below. The changes are in `include/thread_pool.hpp` and `src/thread_pool.cpp`, every public signature is unchanged, and nothing is committed.

## Test results
All builds pass my stress test:

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| TSan with one suppression (10 runs: unpinned, 2 cores, 1 core) | no reports |
| TSan through the real CMake `lib` target, same suppression | no reports |
| ASan/UBSan | no reports |
| Release, pinned to 1 core | passes, no hangs |

The library also compiles without warnings under `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wconversion`. Only GCC 14 was tested, because clang isn't installed here.

## The remaining TSan report
- **When it happens:** without the suppression, most stress runs that made 20,000 throwing tasks gave two warnings. They need a task to throw and the caller to read the exception (e.g. `e.what()`) right after `get()`. In a normal test suite this should be very rare.
- **Why it's a false positive:** a worker has to drop its `std::promise` after publishing the result, and that can free the exception. The ordering that makes this safe is the exception's refcount, which sits inside `libstdc++.so`, where TSan can't see it.
- **Evidence:** a 30-line program with no pool, just `std::thread` and `std::promise`, gives the same report on all 3 runs.
- **Fix for your CI:** the only standard-library workarounds would keep exceptions alive longer in the pool, which is worse than the warning. If your TSan runs read exceptions in a tight loop, add this one line to your TSan suppressions file: `race:std::__future_base::_Result`.

## Bugs found by repeated runs
The first TSan pass was clean; these only showed up on repeat runs and pinned schedules:
- **Deadlock caused by helping:** a waiting task could pull in a task that depended on it, even with another worker idle. Waiters now leave tasks to idle workers. If they run every task themselves, the ping-pong test hangs.
- **Exception freed too early in `parallel_for`:** a leftover helper could free the exception while the caller was reading it. The caller now takes the exception out before rethrowing.
- **Stack overflow risk:** `wait` runs the newest task first, while workers stay first-in, first-out. If `wait` takes the oldest task instead, 300,000 parent tasks waiting on children crash the test.

## Decisions where the header is silent
- `ThreadPool(0)` is treated as 1 worker, and the header now says so.
- After a body throws, `parallel_for` still runs every remaining index, then rethrows the first exception.
- Tasks release their callable and arguments before the future becomes ready, so anything they own is gone by the time `wait` returns.
- `wait` also handles futures from outside the pool: foreign promises are polled every 50 µs to 1 ms, and deferred futures run on the caller.

## Known limits
- **Deadlock with all workers busy:** if `wait` picks up an unrelated task that depends on the waiting task's own progress, the two deadlock. Waiting on a child is safe, but this case can't be ruled out, because a future can't be traced back to its task.
- **`parallel_for` chunking:** when a range is much larger than the thread count (over 8 × (workers + 1) indices), indices run in chunks. A body that blocks waiting on a neighbouring index can therefore hang, so bodies shouldn't depend on each other.
- **Destroying the pool from its own task:** this isn't supported, because a worker can't join itself.

The stress test isn't in the repo because you didn't ask for one. It's at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-hadriensuper-testLLM--work-runs-cpp-threadpool-claude-r1/a6d72343-3250-4021-abb3-35a9db1a6165/scratchpad/test.cpp`, and the pool-free repro is `repro.cpp` in the same folder. That's a temporary folder, so copy them out if you want to keep them.
